rules.summary: Judge whether an abstraction reduces total system complexity.
Assess whether a module mixes unrelated responsibilities.
Judge whether dependencies honor one identified architectural boundary.
Judge the role of one deterministically nominated dependency hub.
Judge whether one class owns unrelated responsibilities.
Judge whether representative behavior changes remain architecturally local.
Judge whether change pressure and structural risk form a maintenance hotspot.
Judge whether component boundaries create a maintainable size distribution.
Measure declared architecture characteristics with executable fitness evidence.
Count cyclic dependencies in the internal Python import graph.
Measure `asyncio.run` calls and enforce a single synchronous boundary.
Count async functions manually pairing created tasks with `gather`.
Count event-loop policy APIs deprecated in Python 3.14.
Count default-executor calls that can usually use `asyncio.to_thread`.
Count the coroutine function alias deprecated in Python 3.14.
Avoid storing an instance cache for a computation independent of that instance.
Avoid retaining object instances in function-wide method caches.
Assess whether continuous integration enforces required gates.
Measure required CI checks meeting the configured feedback target.
Detect registry classes that override their derivable class key.
Count classes whose methods do not follow one explicit source order.
Judge whether inheritance is preferable to composition.
Judge whether an implementation preserves its declared type contract.
Find short tightly named classes that may form one nested namespace.
Forbid singly private class names at module scope.
Count classes that only namespace static or class functions.
Count static methods that hard-code their owner to call a sibling class method.
Count concrete project bases that exist only for one closed-world subclass.
Count project-owned inheritance layers that add only a name or forwarding frame.
Count deterministic MRO hazards among project-owned direct bases.
Count `staticmethod` and `classmethod` calls used without decorator syntax.
Keep retained components as the single source of truth for their attributes.
Count CLI parsers that bypass the configured Cyclopts foundation.
Detect concrete collection parameters that require only an abstract capability.
Count fixed pair sequences whose complete use has unique-key mapping semantics.
Recommend list, tuple, or set only when local use proves interchangeability.
Count explicit calls to the builtin tuple constructor.
Normalize the longest contiguous comment without judging its usefulness.
Classify why a comment exists with a local bounded model.
Judge whether a comment remains accurate beside the current system.
Measure the largest number of loops in one comprehension.
Count fresh sets populated by a loop that can be one set comprehension.
Count hardcoded path-discovery policies in Python collections.
Find project module constants exposed without a leading underscore.
Count project-owned constants imported outside their defining module.
Keep module constants at their earliest dependency-safe top-level position.
Count source references to assets absent from the supplied catalog snapshot.
Count referenced fields absent from an existing data asset schema.
Count explicit source type expectations that disagree with catalog schemas.
Count source references to assets explicitly deprecated or removed.
Count downstream assets exposed to declared breaking schema changes.
Count source references exposed to explicitly unhealthy data dependencies.
Count governed assets missing an owner or required domain.
Measure impacted downstream assets lacking retained test evidence.
Measure cataloged assets and fields lacking a business description.
Count lineage edges whose endpoint is absent from the catalog snapshot.
Count undecorated private module functions without project reference evidence.
Recommend how to obtain and own one capability.
Check whether maintained third-party code should replace custom work.
Measure resolved dependencies lagging their latest compatible release.
Judge whether one candidate fits the required capability.
Count dependencies with an explicit adverse upstream or release state.
Judge the integration effort for one dependency candidate.
Judge whether the project can maintain a dependency fork.
Find repeated unary transformations performed directly by external packages.
Measure dependencies missing facts required by offline version checks.
Assess whether deployment can reproduce one known artifact.
Judge whether a risky deployment verifies behavior before broad exposure.
Judge whether deployment exposure is explicitly bounded.
Judge whether rollout success criteria support a clear decision.
Judge whether a deployment has a usable rollback path.
Classify whether generic values hide repeated domain rules.
Judge whether a design pattern earns its structure.
Judge whether an established variation can grow without destabilizing policy.
Enforce compact self-contained house docstrings where documentation exists.
Require shape and dtype semantics for public tensor callables.
Judge whether consequential engineering decisions remain explainable.
Count exact sibling methods that can be pulled into their shared direct base.
Find repeated string literals that occupy one exact semantic role.
Judge whether similar code duplicates shared knowledge.
Count nonpublic attributes accessed outside their lexical class owner.
Detect explicit enum values that standard `auto()` would preserve.
Detect static string dictionaries that mirror one enum.
Recommend the narrowest shared `enums.py` for reused enum classes.
Require one enum class in each shared `enums` package implementation file.
Prefer public conversions over direct standard `StrEnum` and `IntEnum` values.
Judge whether failures retain useful and safe diagnostic context.
Judge whether failures are handled at a capable boundary.
Judge whether partial failure preserves resource and state integrity.
Count literal local setup assignments needlessly protected by a broad `try`.
Keep each try, except, else, and finally clause narrowly scoped.
Place reused exception classes in the narrowest justified `exceptions.py`.
Detect empty directories after configured exclusions.
Measure Python directory depth below configured source roots.
Measure direct Python modules per directory and flag overcrowded folders.
Measure the largest executable function body and flag hard-ceiling violations.
Count private one-line helpers that have only one local reference.
Count module helpers used exclusively by one class method.
Count positional-only parameters without an observable structural reason.
Judge whether a function stays at one useful level of abstraction.
Judge whether a function makes its material effects apparent.
Count option-like parameters that callers can pass without names.
Find one-line nested functions whose named boundary lacks demonstrated reuse.
Count public unary functions that only forward one argument.
Count one-line public functions and methods without enough behavior or reuse.
Limit explicit `if` branches inside one function or method.
Count absolute imports of modules owned by the importer's project package.
Count imports that cross a project-owned nonpublic boundary.
Detect concrete runtime checks that stand in for a capability.
Judge whether clients depend on a focused contract.
Recommend the smallest Python interface form that fits actual variation.
Detect repeatable project work missing a canonical task.
Count feature flags that lack a current lifecycle decision.
Count direct logger provider calls outside the configured project boundary.
Judge whether a persistent-state migration can be rolled out safely.
Judge whether a migration preserves the required compatibility window.
Judge whether migration verification can detect material data errors.
Judge whether a migration is genuinely reversible or recoverable.
Recommend a Python foundation for one class.
Require one model-shaped class in each shared `models` package implementation file.
Place reused model classes at the narrowest boundary justified by their imports.
Require direct Pydantic models to use an established approved house base.
Count structures that manually repeat fields from one model instance.
Measure the largest Python module and flag a physical-line ceiling.
Measure top-level classes and functions as a deterministic focus proxy.
Find barrel modules that define no behavior beyond re-exporting imports.
Judge whether one Python name should be public or non-public.
Measure observability coverage over declared operational risks.
Judge whether telemetry carries useful and safe diagnostic context.
Measure alerts with enough information for an owned response.
Measure owned user-facing services with defined service objectives.
Measure whether a newcomer can perform essential project work.
Measure operational triggers linked to current executable guidance.
Judge whether critical state can be restored within declared objectives.
Judge whether available backups satisfy the recovery point objective.
Judge whether backups have been verified through a representative restore.
Judge whether verified recovery capability fits declared objectives.
Judge whether a performance decision has adequate profiling evidence.
Judge whether an optimization earns its complexity.
Measure critical performance budgets protected by repeatable regression checks.
Judge whether a benchmark supports the decision made from it.
Judge whether algorithmic growth fits plausible workload bounds.
Find avoidable host, NumPy, or explicit DLPack tensor round trips.
Find model validators that depend on only one declared field.
Find field validators that reimplement built-in Pydantic constraints.
Find model factories that manually reproduce Pydantic field validation.
Find `model_validate` calls that already spell out ordinary constructor fields.
Find optional-field models whose validator proves mutually exclusive variants.
Recommend a model for constructor-heavy validated data classes.
Judge whether a release can be traced through its complete identity.
Judge whether retry behavior improves reliability without amplifying failure.
Judge whether replayable operations control duplicate effects.
Judge whether load can exceed controlled work and resource limits.
Judge whether one failed operation is eligible for automatic retry.
Judge whether retry work stays within an end-to-end budget.
Judge whether retry backoff avoids synchronization and unbounded delay.
Judge whether one change can be reviewed with reasonable confidence.
Measure independently reviewed changes on protected development lines.
Measure security-sensitive boundaries covered by current threat analysis.
Judge whether code and services receive only necessary authority.
Judge whether a project can receive and resolve vulnerability reports.
Require explicit non-expiring SQLAlchemy async session factories.
Find SQLAlchemy session commits nested inside loops.
Prefer SQLModel ``exec`` for exact scalar selections.
Remove scalar extraction repeated after SQLModel ``exec``.
Prefer ``Session.get`` for provable SQLModel primary-key lookups.
Judge whether mutable state has one clear owner.
Judge whether required operation order is explicit and justified.
Count multiline values assembled from adjacent literal fragments.
Select a string mechanism from explicit construction requirements.
Find fixed repeated-string expressions used as decorative separators.
Judge whether tests provide proportionate confidence.
Judge whether tests control state without losing meaningful behavior.
Measure coverage of declared and discoverable failure scenarios.
Count quarantined flaky tests without timely owned remediation.
Count explicit imports of pytest ``conftest`` modules.
Count uses of pytest's legacy ``tmpdir`` fixtures.
Count safe sibling-test groups that differ only in literal values.
Classify whether pytest rejects configuration and marker mistakes.
Classify pytest import isolation from the effective import mode.
Detect conflicting AnyIO and pytest-asyncio automatic modes.
Detect configured coverage that measures statements without branches.
Count direct mutations of module-owned state by collected pytest tests.
Count ``asyncio.run`` calls owned by synchronous pytest tests.
Count async pytest tests without AnyIO or pytest-asyncio ownership.
Limit conditional branches owned by one collected pytest test.
Limit executable statements owned by one collected pytest test.
Count manual literal case loops that should use Pytest parametrization.
Count broad integer ranges that should use a Hypothesis strategy.
Count nested Torch base-two power expressions that obscure a fluid tensor chain.
Detect the deprecated annotations future import for Python 3.14 projects.
Find Boolean annotations that use `None` as a third state.
Keep project and tool Python targets explicit and mutually consistent.
Count prohibited universal types in every Python annotation position.
Count casts and flag structurally repeated cast patterns.
Recommend scoped `typings.py` modules when reusable declarations are scattered.
Find repeated inline constrained annotations that deserve a named type alias.
Count builtin `bool` calls whose operands are already proven Boolean.
Count quality waivers that lack a current bounded justification.
Count exact AI-associated style patterns reported by external analyzers.
Measure how much eligible prose contains AI-associated style evidence.
Measure uniform sentence length without inferring authorship.
Measure uniform paragraph length without inferring authorship.
Measure the share of sentences using one dominant opening word.
Report one eligible detector signal as triage rather than proof.
